about: Named cells of tests/shared/shadows_fixture/generated/shadows/fixture.png (design data, brief M4-03): row 0 is the northern row, column 0 the western column; a cell's centre is E = e_min + 0.25 + 0.5 column, N = n_max - 0.25 - 0.5 row (lv95, 0.5 m cells); local x = E - origin e, z = -(N - origin n) by the fixture's world.json (the owner's axes); value is the PNG's pixel (255 shadow, 0 not); cast and own are the rule's two shadows of the 1 m march cell (row // 2, column // 2), before the inset.

cells.name: behind the block
cells.why: 4 m north of the 10 m block: cast shadow, kept by the inset

cells.name: the shadow's kept edge
cells.why: the eastern half of the 1 m march cell (16, 4) on the shadow's western edge: the 0.5 m inset keeps it, an inset at 1 m would remove the whole cell

cells.name: the shadow's outer edge
cells.why: the western half of the same march cell (16, 4): in cast shadow, removed by the 0.5 m inset

cells.name: the shadow leans east
cells.why: lit: the far end of the block's shadow lies east of its near end, where (41, 7) is shadow

cells.name: south of the block
cells.why: the sun stands south: nothing is cast towards it

cells.name: the thin wall's shadow
cells.why: a 6 m wall one 0.5 m pixel thick: its 1 m cell takes the largest pixel, so it casts

cells.name: the ridge at the east edge
cells.why: in shadow; its neighbour outside the grid does not count, so the edge cell stays

cells.name: the ridge's lit south face
cells.why: a slope of 0.5 facing the sun

cells.name: the slope's last row
cells.why: the grid's southern edge: no point towards the sun is inside the grid, so only its own shadow (one-sided normal, 2 m per m facing away) makes it shadow

cells.name: the slope's western edge
cells.why: in its own shadow, but its western neighbour is lit: removed by the inset
